title: The Cheapest Walk Across a Toll Grid

concept.title: Dijkstra on a grid: the cells are nodes, and the weight of a step is the cost of the cell you step on
body: Every cell of a grid has a toll that you pay each time you **enter** the cell (and also for the starting cell). You may move up, down, left and right. What is the cheapest walk from the top left to the bottom right cell? Because you can go in all four directions, the cheapest walk can go around a very expensive cell, or even backwards, so the simple "only right and down" dynamic programming is not enough.

This is Dijkstra's algorithm on the grid graph. The node is the cell `(x, y)`, and the edge to a neighbour has the weight of the **neighbour's** cost. `dist[x][y]` is the cheapest total toll to be standing on that cell, including its own toll.
The grid has up to 40000 cells and 160000 directed edges, so the heap-based algorithm runs in O(h * w * log(h * w)). The total can reach about 4 * 10^13, so use 64-bit integers.

statement: A grid of `h` rows and `w` columns gives the toll of every cell. You start on the top left cell and want to reach the bottom right cell, moving one step up, down, left or right at a time. You pay the toll of every cell you enter, and also the toll of the starting cell. Print the smallest total toll.
inputFormat: Each of the next `h` lines has `w` numbers: the cost of entering each cell of a row.

examples.note: The walk 1, 3, 1, 1, 1 costs 7; going through the 5 costs more: 7.

hints: Use Dijkstra's algorithm with a heap of (cost so far, row, column).
The weight of a step is the toll of the cell you enter.
The start cell already costs its own toll.

explanation: Dijkstra on the grid graph where a step costs the toll of the cell entered; the distance of the bottom right cell, including the toll of the start, is the answer.
solution.complexity: Time O(h * w * log(h * w)), space O(h * w).

code.python:
import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

h, w = map(int, input().split())
cost = [list(map(int, input().split())) for _ in range(h)]

import heapq
INF = 10 ** 18
dist = [[INF] * w for _ in range(h)]
dist[0][0] = cost[0][0]
heap = [(cost[0][0], 0, 0)]
while heap:
    d, x, y = heapq.heappop(heap)
    if d > dist[x][y]:
        continue
    for p, q in ((x + 1, y), (x - 1, y), (x, y + 1), (x, y - 1)):
        if 0 <= p < h and 0 <= q < w and d + cost[p][q] < dist[p][q]:
            dist[p][q] = d + cost[p][q]
            heapq.heappush(heap, (dist[p][q], p, q))
print(dist[h - 1][w - 1])
